chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Rifāʿah al-Nakhkhās, who said:

I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: I bargained with a man over a bondwoman, and he sold her to me according to my judgment. I took possession of her on that basis, then I sent to him one thousand dirhams and said to him: These are one thousand dirhams according to my judgment over you. But he refused to accept them from me, and I had already touched her before sending him the price.

So he عليه السلام said: I hold that the bondwoman should be appraised with a fair valuation. If her price is more than what you sent to him, then it is upon you to return to him what fell short of the value. And if her price is less than what you sent to him, then it belongs to him.

I said: May I be your ransom, then if I find a defect in her after I have touched her? He عليه السلام said: You do not have the right to return her, but you may take from him the difference in value between soundness and defect.

key_terms.بِالثَّمَنِ: the purchase price due in the transaction
key_terms.بِحُكْمِي: according to my own assessment or valuation in the sale
key_terms.تُقَوَّمَ: she should be appraised and assigned a market value
key_terms.عَيْبًا: a defect diminishing the item’s value
key_terms.فَقَبَضْتُهَا: I took possession of her in a legally relevant manner

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a purchased bondwoman is appraised after delivery and a defect is found after touching her?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on a sale concluded on the buyer’s own valuation, where possession and physical contact occurred before final payment was accepted. The Imam عليه السلام rules that the bondwoman must be appraised fairly, with any shortfall paid to the seller and any excess remaining his, and that after consummating use, the buyer may not return her for a defect but may claim the difference in value.
